key_control_statement: Key control determines practical custody; the protocol does not characterize same-ledger balances as a separate form of custody. The ABI V1 field name custody_domain means accounting control domain only and does not assert possession of user keys.

vocabulary.control_domain: an accounting control domain label on the same ledger; the protocol-controlled scope in which entitlements are reconciled (V1 wire name custody_domain)
vocabulary.controlled_location: atoms held in a protocol-controlled accounting location such as a pool, margin account, escrow, or fee residue bucket (V1 table custody)
vocabulary.controlling_principal: the principal that controls a controlled location (V1 field owner on a custody row)
vocabulary.claimant_entitlement: atoms a claimant may withdraw from a control domain (V1 table liabilities; V1 field owner on a liability row names the claimant)
vocabulary.unencumbered_reserve: named protocol-owned atoms with no claimant (V1 table reserves); never backing for a claimant entitlement
vocabulary.key_controlled_account: self-custody balance controlled by a key (V1 table balances, control domain accounts); never backing for a claimant entitlement
vocabulary.pending_external_obligation: a registered external-delivery row awaiting acknowledgment (V1 table outbox; asset and amount are absent from the V1 row and must come from the sidecar)
vocabulary.terminal_obligation: a claim that must reach a terminal drain or tombstone (V1 table terminal_obligations; control domain and controlling principal are absent from the V1 row)

v1_alias_table.meaning: controlling_principal on custody rows; claimant on liability rows; reserve principal on reserve rows; account key on balance rows
unsigned 128-bit integer atoms at the profile-bound eight-decimal precision
terminal_obligation rows (V1 projection lacks control_domain and controlling_principal)
pending_external_obligation rows (V1 projection lacks asset and amount_atoms)

conservation: sum(balances) + sum(custody) + sum(reserves) = supply per asset; entitlements are claims against custody, never a fourth owned bucket

source_classes.v1_source: custody atoms not matched by an entitlement in the same control domain
outbox row plus sidecar asset and amount
terminal_obligations row plus sidecar control_domain and controlling_principal

exact_one_classification: every controlled source atom is classified exactly once per (asset, control_domain); omission, duplication, and cross-domain assignment reject

arithmetic.residue: carried explicitly as a named reserve row

claimant_backing_guard.precedence_change: Since source commit 85c45bd629f6793e06d995a335ec92fc8a5926e6 the composed guard folds all four tables before evaluating any inequality, so a state whose OPEN-terminal fold overflows and whose entitlements exceed same-domain custody reports CLAIMANT_BACKING_TOTAL_OVERFLOW; before that commit the R1 inequality was evaluated before the terminal fold and such a state reported LIABILITIES_EXCEED_SAME_CONTROL_DOMAIN_BACKING. Both directions fail closed; the change is pinned by the golden vector precedence_terminal_overflow_before_domain.
claimant_backing_guard.custody_fold_overflow: reachable: GlobalEconomicStateV1 validates rows, not supply equality, so custody rows of one asset can sum past u128; pinned by the golden vector rejects_custody_aggregate_overflow

nonclaims: This contract renames nothing on the V1 wire; every V1 field name and byte stays stable and the vocabulary applies to new code, models, and documents only.
The claimant-backing guard proves only the two state-visible necessary inequalities; exact all-lane reconciliation requires the GlobalAccountingAllocationCertificateV1 producers.
No production, release, settlement, verifier, migration, publication, or value-moving authority is granted.
